text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.
notes: Seeds came from the corpus-profile candidate vector-16 (animal venom in medicine); its fenced SQL re-ran unchanged at 4 rows (655153, 714366, 891733, 949830). Dropping the euroSciVoc bucket fence, as a vector question must, the corpus-wide venom family is 12 projects, inside which the only crisp 2-4 member theme is snakebite therapy: 850974 MABSTER and 899670 ADDovenom. Both IN by full text: MABSTER develops recombinant human monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies and designed minibinders to replace animal-derived antivenom; ADDovenom develops ADDobody/ADDomer synthetic scaffolds as antivenom for Sub-Saharan Africa. Pooled k=10 over all four conditions returned 23 distinct projects; 21 rejected. Notable OUTs: 949830 ToxMim (turns venom toxins INTO drug leads for human disease, does not treat snakebite), 654294 TentaclesOfVenom / 845674 EVER / 101031131 SpecSpiderVenom / 748902 VIPS / 841576 Finding VENomS (venom evolution and biodiscovery, no bite therapy), 728647 SOS Jelly (skin cream against jellyfish stings, not snake bite, not an engineered protein therapy), 891733 MITafterVIT and 655153 IgEPath (allergy/immune response to venom, not a treatment for bite victims), 751567 NATRICINE / 101027605 EARtH / 101024700 HeadStrong / 101030356 Snake-eyes / 703438 Evol-Eyes (snake biology and evolution), plus off-topic protein/blood engineering hits (715207 MMA, 637877 PredicTOOL, 834952 BIOIMPROVE, 669768 VESCEL, 877280 HemaXis DX, 770992 BloodVariome, 675111 EVOluTION, 740189 EuroBioTox) and non-biomedical lexical noise (763285 PAHremov, 644090 EuroCPS, 863503 ECBS, 816553 DEGCAE, 656067 NOVENA, 101038087 SPHEROTOX). Completeness sweep: (a) objective/title ILIKE snakebite|snake bite|antivenom|anti-venom|envenom|serpent + title snake|venom -> 19 rows, only MABSTER and ADDovenom are bite therapy; (b) objective ILIKE snake|scorpion|viper|cobra AND toxin|bite|antibod|therap -> 5 rows, the other three (COBRAIN, MES-CoBraD, OPENCORONA) are substring noise on 'cobra'; (c) lexical search over the chunk corpus (covers report text the objective sweeps miss) for 'antivenom snakebite envenoming treatment for snake bite victims' -> MABSTER rank 1, ADDovenom rank 2, no other therapy project. MABSTER's objective states snakebite envenoming kills more than 100,000 victims a year. Reference attribution checked against MABSTER's workPerformed: the spinout Y-king Biologics and the EUR 3 million belong to the patented universal pH-switch for antibodies (Structural biology section), while the nanobody/minibinder pipeline is the thread published in Nature Communications and Nature. term_style paraphrase: the question says remedy, poisonous snakes, poison, blood of animals repeatedly exposed, proteins engineered in the laboratory, while the gold texts say antivenom, snakebite envenoming, venom toxins, immunized/hyperimmunised horses and sheep, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, ADDomer, phage display, neutralise. The matrix agrees: ADDovenom is invisible to lexical (dense 1, hybrid_rerank 1) and MABSTER is only lexical 5 against dense 2 / hybrid 1.

text: Which projects build a microfluidic chip device that carries a working model of the human blood-brain barrier or neurovascular unit, either as the whole chip or as one compartment of a larger organ-on-chip system?
reference_answer: Thirteen projects put a working blood-brain barrier (BBB) or neurovascular unit (NVU) model inside a microfluidic chip, almost all justified by the failure of animal and static in vitro models to predict human drug transport into the brain. Most build a dedicated BBB/NVU device: NVU-Chip recapitulates the human NVU in a single microfluidic device and is the first to incorporate cyclic mechanical strain in a BBB model; NOVACHIP builds a scalable vessel-like BBB-on-a-chip from bioprinted endothelialized capillaries; NeuroVU adds real-time chemical and trans-endothelial electrical resistance sensing to an NVU Organ-on-Chip; SONGBIRD integrates 3D scaffolds carrying blood-brain barrier cells into a microfluidic barrier-on-chip screening platform; SweetBrain, DIANA and BrainChip4MED use NVU and brain-on-a-chip models for disease-mechanism work and for screening drugs and nanocarriers that must cross the BBB. Others reach the same structure from vascular or microfabrication engineering: VESCEL engineers hiPSC blood vessels in microfluidic chips and applies them on-chip to blood-brain barrier function, 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP's 3D-printed microfluidic devices generate and maintain living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier, BBBhybrid two-photon-prints a 1:1-scale biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip model of the brain tumour microenvironment with its blood neurovasculature, and FEBRIS builds 3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks to study blood-brain-barrier disruption in cerebral malaria. A third group carries the barrier as one compartment of a bigger chip: MINERVA's microbiota-gut-brain organ-on-a-chip platform, whose brain compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model, and GUTVIBRATIONS' stacked gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip with a blood-brain layer.
notes: MEMBERSHIP RULE, stated in the question text so it is derivable without these notes: the project's own text must describe (i) a microfluidic or chip-based device that the project itself builds and (ii) a BBB or NVU model living in it; the device rule is by wording, and a BBB/NVU compartment inside a larger organ-on-chip system counts. Scope chosen because the corpus-wide organ-on-chip family (~60 projects by title/objective) has no enumerable boundary, while the BBB/NVU has a small set of literal names. IN (13): 101038093 NVU-Chip (3D microfluidic human NVU, first cyclic strain in a BBB model); 840626 NOVACHIP (scalable 3D BBB-on-a-chip); 832045 BBBhybrid (biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip of the brain tumour microenvironment, hCMEC/D3 endothelium + astrocytes in a microfluidic device); 757444 SONGBIRD (barrier-on-chip built around blood-brain barrier cells in a microfluidic network); 797777 NeuroVU (NVU Organ-on-Chip with sensors); 851765 SweetBrain (human-relevant NVU-OoC); 899431 DIANA (BBB-brain model Chip4D Brain on patented organ-on-chip technology); 101032481 BrainChip4MED (microfluidic brain-on-a-chip recapitulating brain tissue and BBB); 724734 MINERVA (engineered organ-on-a-chip platform whose Brain-compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model - compartment clause); 953201 GUTVIBRATIONS (gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip whose deliverables include a blood-brain layer - compartment clause); 101026717 FEBRIS (3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks, BBB disruption in cerebral malaria); 669768 VESCEL (blood vessels engineered in microfluidic chips; report sub-aim 6 applies the blood vessels on-chip to blood-brain barrier function); 798014 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP (3D-printed microfluidic devices that, with hydrogel bioprinting, generate and maintain over time living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier). OUT with the separating fact: 948088 Mal3D-BBB builds a 3D BBB model of collagen gel with endothelial cells, pericytes and astrocytes, but zero of its 5 chunks contain microfluidic, chip or microphysiological - no chip device, so it fails clause (i); this is the one project the device rule deliberately excludes and it is named here so the boundary is visible. 807015 IM2PACT (iPSC-derived BBB models, zero chunks mentioning microfluidic or chip); 865176 Ctrl-BBB (BBB molecular biology, no chip text); 794726 EFHHBBBMS (its text names no device it builds - the microfluidic chamber appears as a requirement of models used during a secondment, and the fellowship's stated outputs are biological findings; closest OUT under this rule); 739759 BrainChip, 824070 CONNECT, 743909 NOC, 840984 NMJ, 842423 BrainCircuit-on-chip, 658850 Als-on-a-chip (neural or brain tissue chips with no BBB/NVU model); 101003361 GliomaChip, 835227 3DBrainStrom (brain tumour chips, not barrier models); 727641 BioREAD (electrical barrier-quality detector FOR organs-on-chip, builds no BBB model); 840231 PTOoC, 753743 MOOAC, 795754 MTOAC, 762315 B-On-Chip, 884823 PORTable STaNDOuTs, 897025 open-TOP (generic or other-organ organ-on-chip devices; none carries a BBB/NVU term anywhere in its text); 779751 INVICTUS (vessel-on-a-chip for ultrasound cavitation); 750601 CLIMB (supported lipid membrane permeability assay, no cells, no chip model); 115975 ADAPTED, 813294 ENTRAIN, 798505 NanoBBB, 829040 MindGAP, 804229 LIMBo (BBB biology or nanomaterial transport, no chip model). COMPLETENESS SWEEP, two arms over the chunk table so report text is covered: arm 1 (the rule's own predicate) = projects with a BBB/NVU term (blood-brain barrier, blood brain barrier, blood-brain-barrier, neurovascular unit, standalone BBB, brain endothelial barrier) AND a chip term (microfluidic, on-chip, on a chip, microphysiological) -> 33 projects, every one adjudicated. Arm 2 (falsification arm, no chip term required) = BBB/NVU term AND an engineered-model term (in vitro with 3D, perfus, engineered, recapitulat or tubular) -> 26 projects of which 10 carry no chip term at all: 642028 NABBA, 721975 in3, 758887 REACT, 803621 LINCE, 825161 ATHENA, 828837 GLADIATOR, 897678 NeuroMOF, 898170 PiezoMagBBB, 948088 Mal3D-BBB, 964934 NECTAR; only Mal3D-BBB builds an engineered 3D BBB model, and it is excluded by the device clause as stated above, the other nine being nanomedicine, theranostics or assay projects. term_style exact-term: the question reuses the gold texts' literal vocabulary (microfluidic, chip, organ-on-chip, blood-brain barrier, neurovascular unit); lexical ranked NVU-Chip 1, NeuroVU 2, SweetBrain 4, VESCEL 7, BBBhybrid 9. Seven of the thirteen gold appear in the final pooled top-10 (NVU-Chip, NeuroVU, NOVACHIP, SweetBrain, BrainChip4MED, VESCEL, BBBhybrid); DIANA, SONGBIRD, MINERVA, GUTVIBRATIONS, FEBRIS and 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP were established by reading plus the sweep, not by the pool at k=10.

text: Across the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships that set out to explain, in mice, how circuits at the front of the brain keep information alive across a short gap before it is used, what cellular mechanisms do they propose to test?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym, p.fundingScheme, COALESCE(p.title,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(p.objective,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.teaser,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.summary,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.workPerformed,'') AS txt FROM project p LEFT JOIN report_text r ON r.projectID = p.id WHERE p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%') SELECT DISTINCT id, acronym, fundingScheme FROM t WHERE (txt ILIKE '%working memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%short-term memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%short term memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%delay period%' OR txt ILIKE '%memory maintenance%' OR txt ILIKE '%holding in memory%') AND (txt ILIKE '%mice%' OR txt ILIKE '% mouse %' OR txt ILIKE '%rodent%' OR txt ILIKE '% rats %') ORDER BY id

reference_answer: Four of these fellowships propose mouse work on how frontal circuitry keeps information available across a delay, and each names a different mechanism to test. AG-GF trains mice on a texture discrimination task with a delay component and asks which cortical areas carry the trace, combining wide-field mapping, two-photon single-cell imaging of neurons that project top-down from frontal areas to primary somatosensory cortex, and optogenetic perturbation; it reports that during the delay persistent cortical activity sat medio-frontally in active trials. SERWOM and PIANISM both put serotonin (5-HT) at the centre: SERWOM images pyramidal and distinct GABAergic interneuron types while mice run a delayed two alternative forced choice (2AFC) task and manipulates 5-HT release in the dorsal raphe (DR) optogenetically, in a mouse model of schizophrenia, while PIANISM works in acute slices and tests how 5HT receptor activity shapes the persistent firing that outlasts the initial excitatory drive, through TRPC/CAN and voltage-sensitive sodium and calcium currents, in naive and chronic ketamine mice. PFCmap instead treats the wiring itself as the mechanism, using optogenetic single-cell connectivity maps to ask how recurrent networks in the superficial layers of the mouse PFC come to sustain delay-period activity as the animal matures.
notes: FILTER RATIONALE: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' is the structured half (schema_docs lists MSCA-IF and MSCA-IF-EF-ST among the top fundingScheme values). The rest of filter_sql is an enumeration device chosen to cover the paraphrase's semantic scope in BOTH of its parts - the memory-over-a-gap sense ('working memory', 'short-term memory', 'short term memory', 'delay period', 'memory maintenance', 'holding in memory') and the mouse sense ('mice', 'mouse', 'rodent', 'rats') - searched over title, objective, teaser, summary and workPerformed rather than objective/title alone. That widening is what admits 659719 AG-GF, whose objective says 'holding in memory' and whose summary says 'short-term memory maintenance', and which the earlier objective-only device missed. At the runtime the scoped path can only build the fundingScheme half - subject matter is not a filterable column - so the topical and species parts fall to retrieval by design. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 7 survivors re-read from scratch this pass): IN 659719 AG-GF - mice trained on 'texture discrimination with a delay component'; 'During the delay, in contrast, persistent cortical activity was located medio-frontally in active trials'; two-photon single-cell imaging of top-down frontal projection populations plus optogenetic perturbation. IN 888270 SERWOM - mice, 5-HT regulation of PFC GABAergic interneurons, delayed 2AFC read out during the delay period. IN 892772 PIANISM - mouse PFC slices, 5HT modulation of WM-related persistent firing. IN 898460 PFCmap - mouse PFC, optogenetic connectivity maps of the recurrent circuits that sustain delay-period activity. OUT 753296 StressPFCog - proposes how chronic stress and the glucocorticoid receptor degrade PFC-dependent cognition; 'working memory' appears once as one readout in a list ('cognitive flexibility, working memory, and novel object recognition') and no delay, maintenance or sustained-activity language appears anywhere, with the delivered GR result on reversal learning. OUT 841620 H2AH2B_Propagation - 'short-term memory' is a metaphor for fast-turnover histone marks in mouse embryonic stem cells during DNA replication; not brain, not a delay. OUT 844318 NeuroTick - mice do perform 'a complex working memory decision-making task', but the target circuit is the cerebellum, which the project's own summary calls 'a region in the back of the brain', and the aim is sensory prediction and tickling, not holding information in frontal circuits. DISCRIMINATION / FILTER LOAD-BEARING: satisfying projects outside the scheme filter - 758032 MEMCIRCUIT (ERC-STG) records from 'mice performing the same auditory working memory task' and dissects prefrontal persistent spiking with projection-specific optogenetics; 670283 SYNPRIME (ERC-ADG) is rodent synaptic work naming working memory; 949131 Hot-Coal WM (ERC-STG) is primate working memory. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records the species used, the brain region, or the proposed cellular mechanism; all three come only from objective/report text, and the filter alone leaves 7 projects of which 3 are out. COMPLETENESS SWEEP (re-run WITHOUT the '%prefrontal%' requirement that caused the original miss): MSCA-IF projects with rodent vocabulary AND any of delayed response, delayed match, delayed non-match, persistent activity, sustained activity, persistent firing, hold/keep in mind, across a delay, delay activity, mnemonic - searched over the same five text fields, excluding the 7 survivors - returned 8 rows, all read and all out: 707084 VoidTrap (optical trapping of nanoparticles in vacuum), 708295 CA1 layers (hippocampal CA1 episodic memory), 753608 RSCHD (retrosplenial head-direction persistent activity - the nearest miss, but a posterior region and a directional compass trace rather than frontal maintenance of a stimulus), 798617 BRONC (cortical network reorganisation for behavioural switching), 840704 BrownianReactivation (modelling of hippocampal-cortical memory consolidation), 843717 Grolaries (cartilage progenitor cells), 867459 P-appetite (Drosophila feeding), 101025627 MyeSync (hippocampal CA2 myelination). TERM_STYLE: paraphrase - the question uses none of the members' distinctive vocabulary ('working memory', 'WM', 'prefrontal cortex', 'delay period', 'persistent firing', 'short-term memory'); 'front of the brain' and 'keep information alive across a short gap' are deliberate substitutions. In the scoped run over the 7 survivors, dense returned only 3 projects and all 3 are gold (898460 rank 1, 892772 rank 2, 659719 rank 3), while lexical ranks the two non-gold survivors 844318 and 841620 inside its list - so the semantic channel, not borrowed vocabulary, is what selects the gold. DOUBT ON RECORD (disclosed, unchanged from the first pass): SERWOM (888270) and PIANISM (892772) come from the same host lab and their delivered reports restate the aim as spatial attention in the superior colliculus rather than prefrontal working memory; they are IN on what they set out to test, which is what the question asks, and the reference for both is written from their objectives only.
